expect.note: three things: `over_budget` says 60.00s is inside the ceiling and 60.01s is not; `fast` is the only key in WALL_BUDGET_S, checked as a set rather than by listing suites; and `evals.run.main()` itself returns 1 on an over-budget total and 0 on an under-budget one

provenance: the `fast` gate's wall clock went 13s (M2) -> 48.6s (M6) -> 55.4s (M7) -> 67.5s (M8) without one run ever turning red, because ADR-002 Decision 4's 60s ceiling was prose in an ADR and nothing read it. This case has now been falsified twice for the same reason one level up each time, and carries both halves because of it. (1) It first read `sorted(evals/report/*-fast.json)[-1]`; on the fresh clone `.github/workflows/eval.yml` builds, the newest file is always the report the branch committed, so a tree measuring 77.23s still scored 89/89 = 1.000 with the gate green (PR #20 R1). (2) It then graded `evals.run.over_budget` alone, and the five-line block in `main()` that applies it was pinned by nothing: deleting `evals/run.py`'s `if over_budget(args.suite, totals["wall_seconds"]):` left a 79.02s run — 32% over — reporting 90/90 = 1.000 at exit 0 with this case PASSing (PR #20 R8). Watched red before the call-site half was added, with that block deleted from evals/run.py and everything else untouched: `[FAIL] fast-wall-clock-budget`, 89/90 = 0.989 against baseline 1.000, wrong: [{wall_seconds: 79.02, exit: 1, got: 0}] — the under-budget row still returned 0, so the case fails on the run that should have been stopped and not on the one that should not.

triage.note: grades a rule and the place it is applied, because holes have appeared at both. `_main_exit_code` drives the real `evals.run.main()` with `load_cases`/`run_case` stubbed to a single result of a chosen duration — no case runs, no report is written, stdout and stderr are swallowed — so what is graded is the value `main()` RETURNS. One line short of the path CI takes: `evals/run.py`'s `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` tail is what turns that value into a process exit code, `_main_exit_code` calls `main()` in-process and never goes through it, and changing the tail to a bare `main()` would disable this ceiling — and the invariant and regression rules with it — with this case still green (PR #20 R13, Debt T-R13). The suite-key check is a set comparison rather than a row per suite name: rows can only ever cover the suites someone thought to list, and `full` was the one missing when `WALL_BUDGET_S["full"] = 1` was shown to slip through green (PR #20 R11).
triage.not_covered: it grades total wall clock only — a case that gets 10s slower while another gets 10s faster is invisible to it; per-case timings are in every committed report for anyone looking. It does not drive `evals/run.py` as a process, so the module tail described above is ungraded. It does not exercise the `--update-baseline` path, which returns before the ceiling is consulted and reports nothing about it (PR #20 R12, Debt T-R12). And it does not settle what a contributor on slower hardware should do when the ceiling is genuinely unreachable there (PR #20 R6, Debt T-R6).
